On 30 October 2023, the Council unanimously adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 as resolution 2704 (2023), extending the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [VOTE]. The resolution expresses willingness to extend the mandate further based on inter-party agreement [OPERATIVE]. Building on resolution 2694's monitoring of the Government–ELN ceasefire, resolution 2704 contemplates verification of the Government–EMC ceasefire pending Secretary-General confirmation of a ceasefire with appropriate protocols [ADDITIONAL].

Brazil emphasized the resolution reflects Colombia's sovereign will and supported its total peace strategy, hoping the Council could authorize EMC verification when sufficiently mature [BRAZIL]. Speaking for the African members, Ghana welcomed the unanimous extension and supported EMC monitoring contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, while pledging to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people [A3]. Both statements support the Council's willingness to consider the Government–EMC verification scope, provided the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with suitable protocols. This shared ground aligns with the resolution's operative conditions regarding future mandate extensions and specific verification protocols [OPERATIVE][ADDITIONAL].
